description: Rank the whole market on ONE completed interval: pick bar (1d, the default, or 1h on a Pro key), columns, an order_by field and top_n. Answers 'top markets by funding / open interest / returns on the latest day or hour' and 'what percentile is BTC on open interest'. day defaults to the last complete interval; scope defaults to crypto (HIP-3 markets track an underlying that closes, so their flow is not comparable); stat=percentile|zscore ranks within your eligible markets; window_days recomputes the trailing-window fields; min_usd_volume_7d_avg (USD/day at either bar) keeps dust out of the ranking and the ranking is computed after it. Field names come from list_fields — never guess them, they are snake_case compound names and each one lists the bars it exists on; for a cut ('top decile by X') use screen_universe.

bar.description:
`1d` (the default) for completed UTC days, `1h` for completed UTC hours.
An interval, at either grain, is stamped by the instant it **closes** —
an hourly `…T09:00:00Z` is the hour that ended at 09:00.

coins.description:
Restrict to these markets. A market outside your plan's coverage is
ignored rather than widening the answer.

columns.description:
Fields to return per market, from `list_fields`. `coin` is always
included. Defaults to price, traded notional and the interval's return.

day.description:
The day or hour to rank. For `bar: 1d`, `YYYY-MM-DD` or `latest` (the
default: the most recent complete day). For `bar: 1h`, a completed hour
as `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00:00Z` — the hour that *ended* at that instant — or
`latest`.

descending.description: Rank largest first (the default). Set false for the smallest.

min_usd_volume_7d_avg.description:
Drop markets whose average **daily** traded notional over the trailing
window is below this value, in USD/day at either bar — a floor chosen at
`1d` means the same thing at `1h` — so dust cannot top a ranking.

order_by.description:
The field to rank by. Need not appear in `columns`. Defaults to the
interval's traded notional.

scope.description:
`crypto` (the default), `hip3`, or `all`. Restricted markets track an
underlying that closes, so their flow is not comparable on a weekend.

stat.description:
`raw` (the default), `percentile`, or `zscore`. Percentile and z-score
are ranked **within the markets your plan can see**, so they need a
slice of at least four markets.

top_n.description:
How many markets to return, 1..100 (values outside are clamped to the
nearest bound and the response says so). Defaults to 20.

window_days.description:
Recompute the trailing-window fields over this many days, 1..365
(default 7). The response always states the window it used.

name: query_cross_section

as_of.description:
The UTC day (`YYYY-MM-DD`) or completed hour (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00:00Z`) the
answer describes. An interval is stamped by the instant it closes, so an
hourly `…T09:00:00Z` is the hour that ended at 09:00.

bar.description: The grain this answer was computed at: `1d` or `1h`.

bar_age_hours.description:
How many hours ago the newest interval closed. The published hourly source
is written ~1.5–2.5 h after its bar, so `bar_age_hours` is the decision
lag: the bar is already this old before anyone can trade on it.

eligible_count.description:
Markets left after your explicit market filter and any traded-notional
floor — the population the percentile, z-score and deciles were computed
over.

matched_count.description:
Markets that reported the ranked field and passed every filter. This is
the count the rows are drawn from.

published_at.description:
When the newest interval in this answer was actually published (written),
UTC. Absent at the daily grain, whose coverage comes from the manifest
rather than the object's write time. Compare with `bar_age_hours` to see
the publication lag.

scope.description: The market population the ranking ran over.

source.description:
`tessera_daily` or `tessera_hourly` — the clock this answer came from,
never the live market.

stat.description:
The ranking treatment actually applied: `raw`, `percentile` or
`zscore`.

visible_count.description:
Markets in your plan's slice with a row on this interval, before any
filter you passed. This is the universe the answer is a statement about.

title: Query cross-section
